data.why: The app's own 'Load example' button already seeds one matching peak; sample.csv in the repo root belongs to the unrelated Python audit CLI (not the glycan peak format), so a small synthetic mz,intensity panel was written matching the app's parser, with two real composition matches at a few ppm offset (within the 10 ppm default), one unmatched outlier peak, one near-miss at the residue-count ceiling with a 50 ppm offset (outside default tolerance, demonstrating tolerance sensitivity), and one peak with a missing intensity value.

goals: Paste or upload an observed m/z peak list and get back candidate glycan compositions within a chosen ppm tolerance
Set maximum Hex/HexNAc/Fuc/NeuAc/NeuGc residue counts to constrain the composition search space for a given glycan class
Compare proton, deprotonated and sodiated ion models at different charge states to see which adduct/charge explains an observed peak
Identify peaks with no plausible candidate composition versus peaks with multiple indistinguishable candidates
Export the ranked candidate matches as CSV for downstream recordkeeping or further structural work

review.summary: This is a faithful, well-evidenced tree of a single-page glycan composition matcher: the phases follow the README workflow, the features are cut sensibly, and the agent found the repo notes' impossible single-run expectation and the CSV's missing ion-model column. It needs light fixes before filing: the 'reliability' phase overclaims against the README's caveat, t11's label doesn't fit one of its examples, the export node lacks direct evidence, and the 50,000-combination limit is never mentioned.
